scope.description: Observe a postponed ReadIndex request through the Node interface of a wrapped leader whose application has reported applied progress past a committed configuration change without having applied it yet, and then applies that change: the decisive observation is whether any Ready delivers the ReadState for the request once the leader has committed an entry of its term.
assumptions: The wrapped node 1 is a four-voter group {1,2,3,4} whose storage holds ten term-1 entries with the last one removing voter 4, and a persisted HardState committing index 10.

Voter 2 is a bare raft instance whose acknowledgements are delivered; voter 3 is a bare raft instance whose append acknowledgements are held (delayed), and voter 4 is unreachable, so the leader cannot commit under the configuration it still has.

The application consumes Readys, writes entries, hard state and snapshots to the leader's storage, calls Advance (reported applied progress through index 10) and only later calls ApplyConfChange for the change it observed; the campaign and the ReadIndex request are issued through the Node interface.

basis.prefix: Build the wrapped leader over the four-voter fixture, pump its Readys (persisting buffers and calling Advance) without calling ApplyConfChange so that applied index 10 is reported while the tracker still holds voters=(1 2 3 4); campaign through the Node interface and pump until it reports StateLeader at term 2 with its term entry acknowledged only by voter 2; issue ReadIndex with context A and pump; then call ApplyConfChange for the committed removal of voter 4 and pump, recording every ReadState the Readys deliver.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing must be answered once the leader has committed an entry of its term, whichever path performs that commit (raft.go:1550-1554 for the MsgAppResp path, raft.go:2013-2028 for the switchToConfig path), because the helper that discharges the duty is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145).
basis.responsibility: raft (target): the leader accepted the request and is the producer of the answer; the application followed the documented Ready/Advance/ApplyConfChange sequence.

comparisons.description: Premise: the wrapped node became leader at term 2 through the Node campaign path.
Premise: the ReadIndex request issued through the Node interface was postponed (no entry of the leader's term committed yet).
Witness: applying the committed change performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11 with committed_entry_term 2), yet no Ready delivered a ReadState for context A.
Witness: the postponed request is still held after that commit.

before.description: Observe the whole interval of one postponed ReadIndex request for two completion paths on the same 4-node group: a local request answered into leader 1's readStates, and a forwarded request (client to follower 2, follower forwards to leader 1) whose answer must be a MsgReadIndexResp delivered back to node 2. In both paths the application then applies an already-committed configuration change whose resulting configuration performs the leader's first commit of the term.
assumptions: Four voters {1,2,3,4} bootstrapped from a ConfState-only snapshot, log entries 1..9 ordinary and entry 10 the configuration change, HardState{Term:1, Commit:10}, applied index 10 (the application reported applied progress but has not yet called ApplyConfChange for entry 10, which node.go:166-187 permits).
Transport preserves raft's per-message semantics; voter 4 is unreachable and voter 3's append acknowledgements are delayed (message loss/delay).

The forwarded request is produced by delivering MsgReadIndex without a From to follower 2, so follower 2 forwards it to the leader it knows; the forwarded case emits only fwd_-prefixed events so that each prerequisite alias is matched by exactly one case.
excluded: Snapshot-based recovery and asynchronous storage writes.

prefix.before: For each case: build four nodes whose storage is bootstrapped with the case ConfState (voters {1,2,3,4}, or the joint configuration voters {1,2,3} + voters_outgoing {1,2,3,4}), append ten term-1 entries with entry 10 the case configuration change, persist HardState{Term:1,Commit:10} and set Applied=10; elect node 1 with a real MsgHup/MsgVote/MsgVoteResp round (voter 4 unreachable, voter 3's MsgAppResp delayed); deliver the read request (locally to node 1, or to follower 2 which forwards it); apply the committed change at index 10 via applyConfChange; deliver the delayed acknowledgement; run one heartbeat round (tick); finally propose one unrelated entry.

requirement.before: A ReadIndex request that a leader accepts by postponing (raft.go:1363-1368) must be answered once the leader has committed an entry of its term, whichever path performs that commit (raft.go:1550-1554 for the MsgAppResp path, raft.go:2013-2028 for the switchToConfig path), because the helper that discharges the duty is guarded only by committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (raft.go:2127-2145) and the caller's comment states the release is due once the committed index has progressed for the term.

responsibility.before: raft (target): the leader is the producer of the answer for a request it accepted, and switchToConfig is part of raft, not of the application.

before.description: Precondition observation: the leader postponed the received request because no entry of its term was committed (committed_entry_term 1, leader_term 2).

Witness: applying the committed removal of voter 4 performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2 == leader_term), so the postponed request is due to be answered, but it is still pending and no ReadState was produced.
Variant of the same cause: applying the committed zero change left the joint configuration, so the incoming half committed the leader's first term-2 entry, yet the postponed request is still pending.

No repair from the periodic round: two heartbeats are sent with an empty read context (heartbeat_ctx_len 0), the delayed acknowledgement of the previous configuration is already in place (match_3 11), and no ReadState is produced.

Control: an unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request (released_request_ctx A), so the release mechanism works and is reached only through the MsgAppResp commit path.
Control for the joint variant: the postponed request is only released once the unrelated proposal is committed.
Forwarded-path premise: follower 2 (StateFollower, known leader 1) emits MsgReadIndex addressed to leader 1, so the answer owed is a MsgReadIndexResp to node 2.
Forwarded-path premise: the leader postponed the forwarded request because no entry of its term was committed.

Forwarded-path witness: applying the committed change performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11, committed_entry_term 2 == leader_term) yet no MsgReadIndexResp was emitted and follower 2 received no ReadState, so the client's forwarded read stays unanswered.
Forwarded-path control: the unrelated proposal committed by the new configuration releases the postponed request, and only then does follower 2 receive the MsgReadIndexResp (ctx A, index 12).

after.description: Premise: the wrapped node became leader at term 2 through the Node campaign path.
Premise: the ReadIndex request issued through the Node interface was postponed (no entry of the leader's term committed yet).
Witness: applying the committed change performed the leader's first commit of term 2 (committed 10 -> 11 with committed_entry_term 2), yet no Ready delivered a ReadState for context A.
Witness: the postponed request is still held after that commit.

revision_reason: The harness now drives the scenario through the public Node/Ready contract instead of a supplied applied index: the application consumes the wrapped leader's Readys and calls Advance while it is still applying the committed configuration change (node.go:166-187 permits this), campaigns, issues its ReadIndex request, and only then calls ApplyConfChange for that change. The comparisons read the delivered ReadStates and the leader's own status rather than internal fields.
